caption: 01 · GRAMMAR — What makes the image-world recognizable?. Trace light, distance, movement, lens position, setting, casting, color, sequencing, and refusal across a defined body of work. Describe patterns without claiming the house or photographer owns an abstract style.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

caption: 02 · AUTHOR — Who created the photograph?. Preserve photographer, assistants, digital technician, set, styling, model, hair, makeup, retouching, and commissioner records. Under U.S. guidance, do not assume a commission alone answers work-made-for-hire status.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping who created the photograph? within The Photographer Who Defines the House.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 03 · LICENSE — What may the house actually do?. Attach usage media, territory, term, exclusivity, crops, derivatives, credits, embargoes, archive copies, portfolio uses, and approval language. Route ownership and transfer questions to counsel with the executed agreement.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping what may the house actually do? within The Photographer Who Defines the House.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

caption: 04 · MEMORY — Whose archive preserves the house image?. Map negatives or RAW files, selects, contact sheets, captions, model releases, licenses, expiry, publication proofs, and preservation custody. Cultural memory may depend on a record the house does not own.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
